tasks.title: Define the research-system architecture contract
tasks.acceptance: Distinguish the inspected autoresearch baseline from proposed Research Continuum extensions; define the question–hypothesis–evidence graph, study and publication contracts, protected evaluation, domain-adapter seams, durable campaign/recovery model, isolation boundaries, allocation rules, local-first scale gates, cross-lab portability and explicit nonclaims with primary-source grounding.

tasks.title: Convert the vision into an outcome and dependency roadmap
tasks.acceptance: Prepend Wave 0, preserve all original Waves 1–8 and their 24 task IDs, acceptance text, dependency logic and gates, identify capacity and human/hardware/licensing decisions, and define stop, pivot, scale and replan conditions without speculative dates.

tasks.title: Make the next work packet executable and validate the repository plan
tasks.acceptance: Provide a standard-library validation command that checks task identity, status, documentation parity, dependency existence/order, DAG acyclicity, wave coverage and navigation links; prove its negative self-test detects an invalid plan; specify one RC-001 packet that can run locally without paid compute, model weights or dataset downloads.

tasks.title: Analyze and scope the autoresearch baseline
tasks.acceptance: Record the upstream reference, attribution, narrow reproduction target and proposed differences; no superiority claim without tests.

tasks.title: Define budgets, safety and evaluation boundaries
tasks.acceptance: Specify permitted edits/tools, total resource accounting, protected evaluator, holdout access and stop conditions.

tasks.title: Build the durable experiment skeleton
tasks.acceptance: A local synthetic campaign survives restart with unique experiment IDs and explicit invalid/failed states; no model or cloud dependency is required.

tasks.title: Implement bounded workspace execution
tasks.acceptance: Restrict owned paths, processes, network and resources; adversarial escape/write attempts fail under the supported threat model.

tasks.title: Implement the evaluator boundary
tasks.acceptance: Keep test data/code outside producer access and enforce development/final feedback separation and query limits.

tasks.title: Implement atomic result persistence
tasks.acceptance: Crash and duplicate-event tests preserve one terminal result and complete cost accounting without overwriting accepted evidence.

tasks.title: Integrate one small training domain
tasks.acceptance: Use lawful data and a pinned baseline; run/reproduce contracts capture exact code, environment, seeds and metrics.

tasks.title: Add hypothesis and patch proposals
tasks.acceptance: Each proposal includes evidence, control, predicted outcome and falsifier; only accepted bounded patches execute.

tasks.title: Compare autonomous and random search
tasks.acceptance: Run equal-total-budget campaigns, retain all failures and independently rerun every claimed finalist improvement.

tasks.title: Add independent replication and ablations
tasks.acceptance: A fresh worker reruns candidates and removes individual changes to test attribution; report failures.

tasks.title: Control repeated selection and leakage
tasks.acceptance: Limit final holdout queries, separate selection from confirmation and report uncertainty after repeated search.

tasks.title: Build evidence-linked research reports
tasks.acceptance: Every conclusion resolves to sources and experiments; contradictions, null findings and resource totals remain visible.

tasks.title: Add an inference-efficiency domain
tasks.acceptance: Use quality-constrained latency/memory objectives and a protected evaluator; integrate Lean Model Lab only through a versioned contract when available.

tasks.title: Add retrieval or data-selection research
tasks.acceptance: Use lawful corpora, train/development/holdout separation and relevance/quality checks without prompt leakage.

tasks.title: Add a numerical optimization domain
tasks.acceptance: Reproduce a non-LLM numerical benchmark to test genuine adapter generality and domain safety boundaries.

tasks.title: Build the question-evidence graph
tasks.acceptance: Track source versions, hypotheses and contradiction links; reject unsupported citations and stale evidence reuse.

tasks.title: Add bounded campaign allocation
tasks.acceptance: Allocate fixed budgets across hypotheses with simple baselines, starvation controls and explicit stop/pivot decisions.

tasks.title: Evaluate research-policy improvements
tasks.acceptance: Compare new orchestration policies on fresh campaigns with equal cost; keep evaluators and accepted records immutable.

tasks.title: Build a local campaign inspection view
tasks.acceptance: Show question-to-evidence lineage, full costs, failures and stop controls with accessible navigation.

tasks.title: Add isolated remote workers
tasks.acceptance: Use scoped jobs with no inherited personal credentials, explicit budgets and verified cancellation/recovery.

tasks.title: Export portable research packages
tasks.acceptance: Another researcher can inspect and reproduce accepted evidence without the original agent conversation.

tasks.title: Run a blind multi-domain evaluation
tasks.acceptance: Independent evaluators test at least two distinct domains against equal-budget simple baselines and publish all outcomes.

tasks.title: Audit safety and scientific integrity
tasks.acceptance: Test evaluator tampering, prompt injection, runaway cost and unsupported conclusions; resolve material defects.

tasks.title: Prepare a bounded autonomous-research release
tasks.acceptance: State supported domains, actual comparative results, known limitations and maintainer-approved release scope.
